carousels.name: 4 ways p*rn may be costing you your grades (23.3% of med students)

slides.kicker: Int. J. of Psychiatry in Medicine, 2025
slides.title: 4 ways p*rn may be [[costing you your grades.]]
slides.sub: 23.3% of medical students had problematic use — and studied less.

slides.title: Of 614 [[students]]
slides.body: In a 2025 study of 614 medical students in Egypt, 23.3% had problematic p*rn use. They reported fewer study hours and lower test scores — and more stress, anxiety and depression. A link, not proof of cause.

slides.title: Ways [[1–2]]
items: Lost hours — study time quietly turns into p*rn time.
Late nights — tired brains don't learn well.

slides.title: Ways [[3–4]]
items: Broken focus — the urge to check keeps pulling you away.
Stress spiral — falling behind, then using p*rn to cope.

slides.title: Protect your [[study time]]
items: Study away from your room — library, café.
Block p*rn on your laptop before exams.
Use a timer — 50 minutes on, 10 off.
Sleep — it's part of studying.

carousels.name: 5 reasons not to quit p*rn just for her

slides.title: 5 reasons not to quit p*rn [[just for her.]]
slides.sub: Do it for her too. But not only for her.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–2]]
items: If she leaves, the reason leaves. Then p*rn comes back.
Resentment builds — "I'm doing this for you" turns into blame.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: She can't be your blocker. That's not her job.
You'll hide slips to protect her opinion of you.

slides.title: You [[deserve]] it too
slides.body: Better sleep, focus, confidence, honesty. Quitting p*rn is for your whole life — she's one part of it.

slides.title: Make it [[yours]]
items: List 3 reasons that are just about you.
Add her as reason #4.
Own your recovery — your plan, your tools.
Let her support, not supervise.

slides.title: 6 ways p*rn [[wrecks your patience.]]
slides.sub: Instant everything makes real life feel slow.

slides.title: Ways [[1–3]]
items: Instant reward — p*rn is always one tap away.
Endless skipping — nothing gets your full attention.
Low tolerance for boredom.

slides.title: Ways [[4–6]]
items: Frustration with slow progress — gym, work, skills.
Short temper with people who don't move at your speed.
Quitting early on anything that takes weeks.

slides.title: Patience is [[trainable]]
slides.body: Many people say their patience comes back after time away from p*rn. Real life is slower. That's not a bug.

slides.title: Train it [[daily]]
items: Wait 10 minutes before any urge — p*rn, food, phone.
Do one slow thing — read, cook, walk.
Stick with one goal for 30 days.
Notice when you want to skip.
slides.note: Save this and practice waiting today 🔖
